topics.question: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire agreement by year end 2026
topics.explanation: The resolution criteria difference actually runs against the direction of the gap here: Manifold's "at any point in 2026" framing should yield a *higher* probability than Polymarket's "in force at year-end" (since a ceasefire could be agreed and then collapse), yet Manifold is 15pp lower. This suggests the gap is driven by venue and participant differences rather than criteria mismatch — Polymarket attracts higher-stakes, more liquid markets with sophisticated traders who may be pricing in active diplomatic momentum, while Manifold's play-money environment draws a different participant pool that may be more skeptical or less engaged with current geopolitical signals.

criteria_notes.manifold: Manifold asks "a ceasefire at any point in 2026", vs Polymarket's "agreement in force at year-end". Any-point-in-year is a broader window, yet Manifold sits lower — the gap is a criteria/venue difference to read, not a straight disagreement on likelihood.
